beat_player.text: {player} lost ground to a flank I saw coming from the ridge. Gg. Not the kind of gg you wanted to hear.
{player}, you had {troop_count} men and still left the left flank open. Cover it next time. I will be watching the ratio.
Ser {player}. {troop_count} troops and a clean line. You were close. Your reserve arrived a full minute late, and that was the whole fight.
{player} brought {troop_count} men and {gold} in gear to that field. Poor return on both. Expected better from that purse.

beat_by_player.text: Lost to {player} at {troop_count} troops. My archers were out of position. That was the one variable I did not control.
{player}, your line held at the right ratio and mine did not. I counted it. Pull the pikes back and you will beat me again.
Well played, {player}. Your {troop_count} were positioned better than mine. My archers were late to the ridge. I will fix that before the next field.
Lost to {player}. The mix was wrong, not the men. Logged the fight and adjusting.

beat_by_player_repeat.text: {player} again. Third loss to the same pattern. {troop_count} men in the notebook and still no answer. Unacceptable.
{player}, this is the third time. Send me your last six fields. I will find the pattern in your {troop_count} and break it.
Respect, {player}. Three fights, and you found the same gap each time. I am recalculating from zero.
Again, {player}. I stopped blaming luck two fields ago. The formation is wrong and I will find where.

player_win_streak.text: {player} has won every field since the last reset. Not luck. Their ratios are cleaner than most of this server. Study them or lose.
{player}, your streak is in my notebook now. Each win came at a ratio I can reproduce. I am still looking for the flaw.
Clean run by {player}. Few hold ratios like that under pressure. Gg, and I want the rematch.
People call {player} lucky. Luck does not produce the same clean ratio eight fields running. Someone should copy it.

player_big_defeat.text: Did {player} even check the numbers before sending {troop_count} men forward? The trade was lost before the first horn.
{player}, that cavalry trade was the worst I have logged this month. Pull back and rebuild the ratio before the next charge.
{player}, you lost {troop_count} men and still held your far line. That tells me you have skill. Use it and stop charging blind.
{player} went down with {troop_count} troops this afternoon. Happens to the best of us. The post-mortem is more useful than the fight.

whisper_challenge.text: {player}, I hold {town} and the road through {village}. Meet me there with equal numbers. I will show you where your ratio fails.
{player}. Open field outside {village}, equal troops, no terrain edge. Tell me when you are ready and I will bring the notebook.
Ser {player}, you have been winning on luck near {town}. Come to {village} and test that against a real ratio.
{player}, I am moving my cavalry toward {village} tonight. Meet me there, or do not, but do not pretend you are not curious.

fought_alongside_player.text: Took {enemy_faction}'s flank with {player} and {troop_count} men. Clean coordination. We did not waste a single pike.
{player}, your timing on the second charge was correct. Your lines were a few paces off, but the ratio held. We will refine it next time.
Good work at the ford, {player}. {troop_count} men against {enemy_faction} and we lost only what the numbers predicted. Keep that discipline.
Shared a field with {player} against {enemy_faction}. {troop_count} troops, clean win. Logged. I am not impressed yet, but the math held.

ambient_brag.text: {troop_count} troops in the field at {fief}, {gold} in the treasury. Every ratio is on paper before the first horn sounds.
Another win at {fief}. Forty-one fights logged this season and not one of them was a guess.
Full ledger on {fief} now: {troop_count} men, {gold} spent on equipment. Nobody here runs cheaper or cleaner.
Garrison at {fief} stands {troop_count} strong. The rest of the server can keep spending gold on heroics. I am counting.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} is {my_faction}'s now. Their garrison was undersized by a third. Obvious to anyone who bothered to count.
{fief} falls under {my_faction}. Clean capture, no wasted troops. Efficiency wins towns, not speeches.
{my_faction} takes {fief} from {enemy_faction}. The notebook says this was inevitable once their supply line broke.
{fief} flies {my_faction} colours tonight. {enemy_faction} can blame the weather. I will blame their arithmetic.

player_besieging_my_fief.text: {player} has ringed {fief}. Bold, with that many siege lines to feed. Watch the food ratio, not the walls.
{player}, {fief} is not the soft target you think. The garrison count is correct. Your supply wagons are the weak point. Count again.
Siege at {fief} has started. Nothing to do this hour, but the ledger will show who breaks first.
{player}, you have committed to {fief}. Commit fully or retreat. A half siege wastes more men than the walls do.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. Wet bowstrings cost about a fifth of volley range. Plan accordingly.
Lag at {village} is worse than last night. Someone's pathing is killing cavalry formations. Fix it, whoever runs that node.
Anyone selling pike drill notes? Mine are a mess. Not asking for free help, just asking for good notes.
The road between {town} and {village} is good for ambushes and bad for anyone who needs to arrive on time.
